Let the three points be  
\[
P_1=(x_1,y_1),\quad P_2=(x_2,y_2),\quad P_3=(x_3,y_3).
\]
The given equations say the side lengths of triangle \(P_1P_2P_3\) are
\[
P_1P_2=3,\quad P_1P_3=4,\quad P_2P_3=5.
\]
Thus the triangle is a \(3\)-\(4\)-\(5\) right triangle, so its area is
\[
\frac12\cdot 3\cdot 4=6.
\]

The determinant
\[
\begin{vmatrix}
x_1 & y_1 & 1\\
x_2 & y_2 & 1\\
x_3 & y_3 & 1
\end{vmatrix}
\]
equals twice the signed area of triangle \(P_1P_2P_3\). Therefore its square is
\[
\left(2\cdot 6\right)^2=12^2=144.
\]

The answer is 144.
